eyebrow: An Open-Source Marvel — The WLED Installer!
welcome: Ladies and gentlemen! Presenting the WLED Web Installer — the marvel of modern science!
uiMode: Select Your Mode, If You Please:
uiModeHint: The Simple Affair keeps things delightfully uncomplicated: choose a version and install at 4MB. For the full spectacle - flash size, memory type, flash mode, and HUB75 layout - step right up to the Grand Production!
unsupported1: Alas, dear listener! Your browser is not yet among the supported!
unsupported2: We implore you - try Chrome or Edge, upon a desktop machine!
unsupported3: The binary files, ladies and gentlemen, await you here:
loadError1: A most unfortunate turn of events! The WLED version list could not be fetched from GitHub!
loadError2: Do check your connection and reload the page, or procure a binary file by hand:
proxyBlocked1: Firmware downloads, I regret to announce, are blocked for this very connection!
proxyBlocked2: This installer fetches firmware by way of download.wled.me, WLED’s own official CORS-enabled relay station - some obstruction upon this network or browser (an ad-blocker! a firewall! a DNS filter, perhaps!) is barring the way, and so installing at this moment would inscribe faulty data upon your device!
proxyBlocked3: Do try disabling any ad-blocker or VPN for this page, or consult your network’s firewall regulations!
proxyBlocked4: You may still procure a binary file by hand, dear listener:
checkingProxy: One moment, please - verifying the firmware download is in working order…
step1-1: Connect your ESP to a USB port, if you would be so kind. We shall install WLED
step2: Press “Begin The Installation!” and select the correct COM port - a simple matter, indeed!
serialHelp1: You may be lacking the drivers for your board, dear listener.
serialHelp2: Behold - drivers for the chips commonly found in ESP boards:
serialHelp3: Do ensure your USB cable is capable of data transfer, not merely power!
chip1: CP2102 (the square chip, if you please)
chip2: CH34x (the rectangular chip, if you please)
step3: WLED, installed and connected, in under three minutes! A marvel, truly!
flashSizeHint: Choose the flash size befitting your board - consult the chart above to learn which chip families employ which size!
layoutHint: Choose the board matching your HUB75 arrangement - consult the chart above for the chip and flash size required!
memoryTypeHint: A matter of consequence only if your board possesses PSRAM - choose the option matching its interface! Leave upon Standard if uncertain, or should your board possess none at all.
flashModeHint: The Default selection matches the flash mode this release’s standard build already employs for each chip - the safest choice, and a necessity to match an existing bootloader when updating in place! DIO and QIO compel that very mode, where a matching release build exists - consult the chart above to learn which chips this presently concerns!
